summary: Training volume over the last 4 weeks has been very low and inconsistent, with only 9 sessions logged, no cycling except one long ride, and sleep quality that is frequently poor (multiple nights under 5 hours and body battery readings regularly below 40). The one run showing HR of 179 bpm at 5:02/km pace signals a significant intensity spike well above aerobic targets, while the open-water swims are well below the 1:50/100m Ironman target pace. Recovery metrics are a persistent concern and likely the root cause of the erratic training pattern.
suggestions: Prioritise sleep consistency above all else — multiple nights of under 4.5 hours are hampering adaptation and increasing injury risk; aim for a non-negotiable 7-hour minimum before any quality session.

Cap running intensity strictly at Z2 (HR under ~145 bpm, pace 6:15–6:45/km) for the next 3 weeks to rebuild aerobic base needed for the sub-4h marathon; the 179 bpm effort on 2026-07-18 was counterproductive given the low overall volume.

Add a dedicated Tuesday pool swim session immediately (Week 6 currently has no swim until Friday) to start hitting the 2×/week swim frequency needed to close the gap toward the 1:50/100m Ironman target.

Treat the Week 6 Thursday evening cycling session as the priority workout of that day — complete the gym session first at reduced volume (25–30 min) rather than a full 60 min to avoid arriving at the bike block already fatigued.

Given the body battery reading of 0–1 on 2026-07-30 (today), treat the Thursday strength session as optional light core only and do not attempt the evening cycling block at full Z2–Z3 effort; a partial recovery day now protects the critical weekend long ride and run.
